transcript.text: Alright, let's get started. We're here to discuss the production rollout of the dependency-upgrade bot. As I understand it, the bot has completed its trial on two repositories without producing a failed build, and it can already open pull requests automatically against repos in our engineering org. Before we enable it across all repositories, we need to go through our final build, security, and operations checklist. I'd like to hear from everyone on where we stand on each of those fronts before I make a decision on the rollout policy.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: This morning I was investigating an unrelated CI queue delay and found that each dependency-upgrade pull request consumes two shared runner slots. We have 20 slots total. To preserve four slots for ordinary developer builds, the bot must have no more than eight open pull requests at once. I haven't updated the rollout proposal with this yet, but it's an important operations constraint we need to account for before enabling the bot across all repositories.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a security constraint. About an hour ago, I received legal's confirmed license decision during a security review: the bot may merge dependencies under MIT, BSD-2-Clause, or Apache-2.0 licenses, but any other license must be blocked and any copyleft dependency must receive manual security review. I have not yet added this decision to the bot configuration ticket, so we need to make sure this license filtering is implemented before the bot is enabled across all repositories.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for surfacing these constraints. So far we have two critical items to address before rollout: Mateo, you've identified that each bot PR consumes two of our 20 shared runner slots, meaning we need to cap the bot at no more than eight open PRs at once to preserve four slots for developer builds. Aisha, you've flagged that legal has confirmed a license policy — the bot may only merge MIT, BSD-2-Clause, or Apache-2.0 dependencies, with all other licenses blocked and copyleft dependencies requiring manual security review — and this filtering hasn't been added to the bot configuration yet. Before I make a decision on the rollout policy, I'd like to hear from anyone else on the build, security, or operations front. Are there any other constraints or checklist items we need to address?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I can speak to the build and operations front. On the operations side, the eight-PR cap I mentioned is the key constraint — I'll make sure to update the rollout proposal with that limit once we wrap up here. On the build side, the trial on two repositories completed without any failed builds, which is a good sign. However, I'd want to confirm that the bot's concurrency limit is actually enforced in its configuration before we go live, so that it cannot exceed eight open PRs simultaneously. That's a concrete checklist item I can own. I don't have any additional build or security constraints beyond what Aisha has flagged on the license filtering side. Are there any other checklist items from anyone else before we finalize?
